Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Rails 8.1 application using SQLite (`storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, Turbo, Stimulus, and Solid Cable / Solid Cache / Solid Queue (all configured to store data exclusively under `storage/` with zero external service calls).

## Boot & Production Serving (`bin/serve`)

- `bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` and `PORT` (default `3000`), precompiles assets (`bin/rails assets:precompile`), prepares SQLite databases (`bin/rails db:prepare`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP is used (`config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`) and all hostnames are accepted (`config.hosts.clear`).
- `GET /up` serves the public health check (`200 OK`).
- Every route under `/moderate` inherits from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic Authentication against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]`.

## Data Model & Quiz Export / Import

- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required, whitespace-normalized). Has many `questions` ordered by `(position, id)` and `active_questions` (`where(active: true)`).
  - `Quiz#as_export_json` / `Quiz#to_export_json` exports strictly `{"title", "questions" => [{"text", "active", "options" => [{"text", "correct"}]}]}` in order, with no database IDs, timestamps, or runtime session/game data.
- `QuizImport` (`app/models/quiz_import.rb`): parses and validates quiz JSON (`active` defaults to `true`, `correct` defaults to `false`, enforcing all question form rules) and creates the new `Quiz`, `Question`s, and `Option`s atomically inside a single database transaction.
- `Question` (`questions`): belongs to `quiz`; `body` (required), `active` (boolean, default `true`), `position` (integer). Has many `options` ordered by `(position, id)`.
  - `Question#save_with_option_rows` skips blank option rows, validates at least 2 non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and at least 1 correct non-empty option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`), and atomically replaces options in a transaction while preserving submitted rows in-memory on validation failure.
  - `move_up!` / `move_down!` swap `position` with the adjacent question in a transaction.
- `Option` (`options`): belongs to `question`; `body` (required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer).

## Frontend & Design System (`quizzy.css`)

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` come directly from `docs/mockups/`.
- Note for future releases: `quizzy.css` already includes pre-built styles for upcoming features:
  - **Big-screen presentation**: `.cover`, `.cover--blue`, `.cover--night`, `.screen`, `.screen-controls`, `.lobby`, `.qr`, `.counter-pill`, `.stage-question__*`, `.stage-options`, `.stage-option.is-correct`, `.leaderboard`, `.leader.is-winner`.
  - **Mobile participant play**: `.play`, `.play-options`, `.play-option`, `.play-status--right`, `.play-status--wrong`, `.result-card`, `.winner-banner`, `.join-form`, `.waiting`, `.waiting__gem`.
  - **Moderator responses**: `.tabs`, `.tab`, `.mark`, `.response-options`, `.response-option`, `.runs-table`, `.badge--running`, `.badge--finished`.
- Stimulus controllers:
  - `option-rows` (`app/javascript/controllers/option_rows_controller.js`): dynamically adds/removes and renumbers option rows (`Option N` / `Option N is correct`) on the question form.
  - `active-toggle` (`app/javascript/controllers/active_toggle_controller.js`): immediately persists `Active` checkbox changes via `fetch(..., { keepalive: true })` and updates active counts/numbering in-place.
- Moderator Preview (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show`): stateless `GET`-driven flow through `quiz.active_questions` in order without writing any database or session state.

        options.create!(
          body: row[:body],
          correct: row[:correct],
          position: idx + 1

    end

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789".chars.freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5
  ONLINE_TTL = 35.seconds

  belongs_to :quiz
  belongs_to :current_game_question, class_name: "GameQuestion", optional: true
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def online_players
    players.where(online: true).where("last_seen_at > ?", ONLINE_TTL.ago)
  end

  def online_players_count
    online_players.count
  end

  def answered_players_count
    current_game_question ? current_game_question.answers.count : 0
  end

  def moderator_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:moderator"
  end

  def players_stream_name
    "game:#{id}:players"
  end

  def player_private_stream_name(player_id)
    "game:#{id}:player:#{player_id}"
  end

  def moderator_token
    Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderator_game).generate(id)
  end

  def start!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      return false unless lobby?

      active_qs = quiz.active_questions.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
      now = Time.current

      if active_qs.empty?
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          started_at: now,
          finished_at: now,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      else
        game_questions.destroy_all
        created_gqs = active_qs.each_with_index.map do |question, idx|
          game_questions.create!(
            question: question,
            position: idx + 1,
            opened_at: idx.zero? ? now : nil
          )
        end
        first_gq = created_gqs.first
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: 0,
          current_game_question: first_gq,
          started_at: now,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      end
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def finish_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_open?

      current_game_question&.update!(closed_at: Time.current)
      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def next_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_closed?

      current_pos = current_game_question&.position.to_i
      next_gq = game_questions.find_by(position: current_pos + 1)

      if next_gq
        next_gq.update!(opened_at: Time.current)
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: next_gq.position - 1,
          current_game_question: next_gq,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      else
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          finished_at: Time.current,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      end
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def end_quiz!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      return false if finished?

      now = Time.current
      current_game_question&.update!(closed_at: now) if current_game_question && current_game_question.closed_at.nil?
      update!(
        status: "finished",
        finished_at: now,
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, option_id:, game_question_id: nil)
    saved_option_id = nil
    counter_changed = false

    with_lock do
      return nil unless question_open?

      gq = current_game_question
      return nil unless gq
      return nil if game_question_id.present? && gq.id != game_question_id.to_i

      option = gq.question.options.find_by(id: option_id)
      return nil unless option

      now = Time.current
      player.update_columns(online: true, last_seen_at: now)

      answer = gq.answers.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id)
      is_new_answer = answer.new_record?
      answer.game = self
      answer.question_id = gq.question_id
      answer.option = option
      answer.answered_at = now
      answer.save!

      saved_option_id = option.id
      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1)
      counter_changed = is_new_answer || true
    end

    if saved_option_id
      broadcast_counters!(bump_version: false) if counter_changed
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        player_private_stream_name(player.id),
        {
          type: "picked",
          game_question_id: current_game_question_id,
          picked_option_id: saved_option_id
        }
      )
    end

    saved_option_id
  end

  def broadcast_counters!(bump_version: true)
    if bump_version
      Game.where(id: id).update_all("state_version = state_version + 1")
    end
    reload

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      moderator_stream_name,
      {
        type: "counters",
        status: status,
        state_version: state_version,
        online_players_count: online_players_count,
        answered_count: answered_players_count
      }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_state!
    reload
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, moderator_state_payload)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(players_stream_name, public_player_broadcast_payload)
  end

  def moderator_state_payload
    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      online_players_count: online_players_count,
      answered_count: answered_players_count
    }

    if (question_open? || question_closed?) && (gq = current_game_question)
      question = gq.question
      opts = question.options.to_a
      total = game_questions.count

      payload[:game_question_id] = gq.id
      payload[:question_number] = gq.position
      payload[:total_questions] = total
      payload[:is_last_question] = (gq.position >= total)
      payload[:question_body] = question.body

      if question_open?
        payload[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          {
            id: opt.id,
            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body
          }
        end
      else
        counts = gq.answers.group(:option_id).count
        total_answers = counts.values.sum
        payload[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          cnt = counts[opt.id] || 0
          share = total_answers.positive? ? ((cnt.to_f / total_answers) * 100).round(1) : 0
          {
            id: opt.id,
            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body,
            correct: opt.correct?,
            count: cnt,
            share: share
          }
        end
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def public_player_broadcast_payload
    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      quiz_title: quiz.title
    }

    if (question_open? || question_closed?) && (gq = current_game_question)
      question = gq.question
      opts = question.options.to_a
      total = game_questions.count

      payload[:game_question_id] = gq.id
      payload[:question_number] = gq.position
      payload[:total_questions] = total
      payload[:question_body] = question.body

      if question_open?
        # Strictly exclude correctness while question is open!
        payload[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          {
            id: opt.id,
            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body
          }
        end
      else
        payload[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          {
            id: opt.id,
            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body,
            correct: opt.correct?
          }
        end
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def player_state_payload_for(player)
    payload = public_player_broadcast_payload.dup
    payload[:joined] = player.present?
    payload[:player_name] = player&.name

    if player.present? && (question_open? || question_closed?) && (gq = current_game_question)
      payload[:picked_option_id] = gq.answers.find_by(player_id: player.id)&.option_id
    end

    payload
  end

  private

  def option_letter(index)
    index < 26 ? ("A".ord + index).chr : (index + 1).to_s
  end

  def assign_code
    return if code.present?

    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      unless Game.exists?(code: candidate)
        self.code = candidate
        break
      end
    end
  end
end

class GamePlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    token = cookies.signed["quizzy_player_#{@game.code}"]
    @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil

    stream_from @game.players_stream_name

    if @player
      stream_from @game.player_private_stream_name(@player.id)
      @player.register_connection!(connection_uid)
    end

    transmit(@game.reload.player_state_payload_for(@player))
  end

  def ping
    return unless @player

    @player.reload.touch_presence!(connection_uid)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    nil
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @player

    @player.reload.unregister_connection!(connection_uid)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    nil
  end
end

class LiveGameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do

    ])
    @q3_inactive = create_question(@quiz, "Draft question?", active: false, options: [
      { body: "Draft A", correct: true },
      { body: "Draft B", correct: false }
    ])
    @q4_multi = create_question(@quiz, "Which are transport protocols?", active: true, options: [
      { body: "TCP", correct: true },
      { body: "JSON", correct: false },
      { body: "UDP", correct: true }
    ])
  end

  test "a quiz can be played many times with independent players and answers, and export omits game data" do
    game1 = @quiz.games.create!
    game2 = @quiz.games.create!

    assert_not_equal game1.code, game2.code
    assert_match(/\A[A-Z0-9]{5}\z/, game1.code)
    assert_equal "lobby", game1.status

    alice = game1.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    bob = game2.players.create!(name: "Bob")

    game1.start!
    game2.start!

    opt_429 = @q2_active.options.find_by!(body: "429")
    opt_418 = @q2_active.options.find_by!(body: "418")

    game1.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: opt_429.id)
    game2.submit_answer!(player: bob, option_id: opt_418.id)

    assert_equal 1, game1.players.count
    assert_equal 1, game2.players.count
    assert_equal opt_429.id, game1.player_state_payload_for(alice)[:picked_option_id]
    assert_equal opt_418.id, game2.player_state_payload_for(bob)[:picked_option_id]

    exported = @quiz.as_export_json
    assert_equal [ "questions", "title" ], exported.keys.sort
  end

  test "games skip inactive questions, track last pick, and end after last active question" do
    game = @quiz.games.create!
    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    bob = game.players.create!(name: "Bob")

    assert_equal 2, game.online_players_count

    game.start!
    assert game.question_open?

    mod_state = game.moderator_state_payload
    assert_equal 1, mod_state[:question_number]
    assert_equal 2, mod_state[:total_questions]
    assert_equal false, mod_state[:is_last_question]
    assert_equal "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?", mod_state[:question_body]

    opt_418 = @q2_active.options.find_by!(body: "418")
    opt_429 = @q2_active.options.find_by!(body: "429")

    # Alice picks 418 then changes to 429; last pick counts
    game.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: opt_418.id)
    assert_equal 1, game.answered_players_count
    game.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: opt_429.id)
    assert_equal 1, game.answered_players_count

    game.finish_question!
    assert game.question_closed?

    # Answers after finish are ignored
    assert_nil game.submit_answer!(player: bob, option_id: opt_418.id)

    counts_by_body = closed_mod[:options].to_h { |o| [ o[:body], o[:count] ] }
    assert_equal({ "418" => 0, "429" => 1, "503" => 0 }, counts_by_body)

    # Next advances directly to @q4_multi (skipping @q3_inactive)
    game.next_question!
    assert game.question_open?
    mod_q2 = game.moderator_state_payload
    assert_equal 2, mod_q2[:question_number]
    assert_equal 2, mod_q2[:total_questions]

  end

  test "player connection presence handles multi-tab connections and editing questions after games" do
    game = @quiz.games.create!
    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice")

    alice.register_connection!("tab-1")
    alice.register_connection!("tab-2")
    assert_equal 1, game.online_players_count

    # Closing one tab keeps Alice online because tab-2 is still open
    alice.unregister_connection!("tab-1")
    assert_equal 1, game.online_players_count

    # Closing the second tab marks Alice offline
    alice.unregister_connection!("tab-2")
    assert_equal 0, game.online_players_count

    # Re-opening marks Alice online again
    alice.touch_presence!("tab-3")
    assert_equal 1, game.online_players_count

    # Editing or deleting questions/quizzes after a game with answers succeeds cleanly
    game.start!
    game.submit_answer!(player: alice, option_id: @q2_active.options.first.id)

    assert @q2_active.save_with_option_rows(

      active: true,
      option_rows: [

        { body: "New B", correct: false }
      ]
    )
    assert_nothing_raised { @q4_multi.destroy! }
    assert_nothing_raised { @quiz.destroy! }
  end

  private

  def create_question(quiz, body, active:, options:)
    q = quiz.questions.new
    assert q.save_with_option_rows(body: body, active: active, option_rows: options)
    q
  end
end

AND we can expose `connection_cookies` on `ApplicationCable::Connection`!

Think about the implications! Exposing a `def signed_cookie(key); cookies.signed[key]; end` method on `ApplicationCable::Connection` immediately makes cookie lookup within `GamePlayerChannel` function seamlessly. And, passing a signed `player_token` from the server-rendered DOM works EVEN IN BROWSERS WITH STRICT COOKIE PARTITIONING on WebSockets. This is huge!

But then I thought about edge cases, like what happens if a player joins via a `POST /play/:code/join` request, the `/play/:code` page renders, and the user closes the tab in milliseconds *before* the WebSocket even subscribes. The `player_connections` table is empty! That's when I thought about Chromium's `bfcache` and that navigation to `about:blank`.

Hold on! What does modern Chromium do with WebSockets and `bfcache`? In most cases, pages with active WebSockets bypass `bfcache`. However, we have to be sure it always happens. So, just in case, we can add a `pagehide` listener inside `play_game_controller.js`: `window.addEventListener("pagehide", () => { this.disconnect() })`. This forces the WebSocket to unsubscribe and disconnect immediately when `pagehide` fires – even if Chromium is considering `bfcache`.

class GamePlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    unless @game
      reject
      return
    end

    token = connection.signed_cookie("quizzy_player_#{@game.code}")

  end

  def ping
    return unless @player

  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound

  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @player

    @player.reload.unregister_connection!(connection_uid)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound

end

# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Rails 8.1 application using SQLite (`storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, Turbo, Stimulus, Action Cable (Solid Cable in production), Solid Cache, and Solid Queue (all configured to store data exclusively under `storage/` with zero external service calls).

## Boot & Production Serving (`bin/serve`)

- `bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` and `PORT` (default `3000`), precompiles assets (`bin/rails assets:precompile`), prepares SQLite databases (`bin/rails db:prepare` across `primary`, `cache`, `queue`, and `cable`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP is used (`config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`), all hostnames are accepted (`config.hosts.clear`), and Action Cable origin forgery checks are disabled (`config.action_cable.disable_request_forgery_protection = true`) so HTTP and WebSockets accept any `Host` / `Origin`.
- `GET /up` serves the public health check (`200 OK`).
- Every route under `/moderate` inherits from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic Authentication against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]`.

## Data Model

- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required, whitespace-normalized). Has many `games`, `questions` ordered by `(position, id)`, and `active_questions` (`where(active: true)`).
  - `Quiz#as_export_json` / `Quiz#to_export_json` exports strictly `{"title", "questions" => [{"text", "active", "options" => [{"text", "correct"}]}]}` in order, with no database IDs, timestamps, or runtime session/game data.
- `QuizImport` (`app/models/quiz_import.rb`): parses and validates quiz JSON (`active` defaults to `true`, `correct` defaults to `false`, enforcing all question form rules) and creates the new `Quiz`, `Question`s, and `Option`s atomically inside a single database transaction.
- `Question` (`questions`): belongs to `quiz`; `body` (required), `active` (boolean, default `true`), `position` (integer). Has many `options` ordered by `(position, id)`.
- `Option` (`options`): belongs to `question`; `body` (required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer).
- `Game` (`games`): belongs to `quiz`; `code` (unique 5-char uppercase alphanumeric code), `status` (`"lobby"`, `"question_open"`, `"question_closed"`, `"finished"`), `current_question_index`, `current_game_question_id`, `state_version` (monotonic counter), `started_at`, `finished_at`.
  - `start!` snapshots `quiz.active_questions` in order into `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`: `position` `1..N`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`), skipping inactive questions.
  - `finish_question!`, `next_question!`, and `end_quiz!` advance game state under `with_lock` and broadcast synchronously over Action Cable.
- `Player` (`players`): belongs to `game`; `name` (required, whitespace-normalized), `token` (secret token stored in signed HTTP-only cookie `quizzy_player_<CODE>` so reopening `/play/<CODE>` in the same browser continues as the same player), `online` (boolean), `last_seen_at`.
  - `PlayerConnection` (`player_connections`): tracks active WebSocket `connection_uid`s per player so multi-tab sessions stay online until all tabs disconnect (`unsubscribed` + `pagehide` teardown + `ONLINE_TTL` heartbeat).
- `Answer` (`answers`): unique per `(game_question_id, player_id)`; stores `option_id` and `answered_at` (updating in place when a player changes their pick while the question is open so the last pick counts).

## Live Game Channels & Frontend

- **Security**: While `status == "question_open"`, player HTML (`GET /play/:code`), JSON (`GET /play/:code/state`, `POST /play/:code/answer`), and shared WebSocket broadcasts (`game:<id>:players`) strictly omit `correct` flags; correctness is only exposed after `finish_question!`. `GameModeratorChannel` requires a `MessageVerifier`-signed `moderator_token` issued only on `/moderate` pages.
- **QR Code**: Generated server-side via `rqrcode` (`ApplicationHelper#render_qr_svg`) as a self-contained inline `<svg>` encoding the full join URL (`http://<host>:<port>/play/<CODE>`).
- **Conference Wi-Fi Resilience**: Stimulus controllers (`moderator-game` and `play-game`) combine live Action Cable WebSocket streams with monotonic `state_version` guards, automatic state resync on `connected()`, `visibilitychange`, `online`, and `pageshow` (`bfcache`), answer `fetch` retry with `AbortController`, and a 2s `/state` fallback poll whenever the WebSocket is disconnected.
EOF

We have implemented the live game feature for Quizzy across both the moderator big screen and participant mobile screens:

- **Data Model & Game Lifecycle**: Added `Game`, `GameQuestion`, `Player`, `PlayerConnection`, and `Answer` models so quizzes can be played multiple times with independent players and answers while skipping inactive questions.
- **Moderator Big Screen**: Added the `"Start a game"` button on the quiz page, opening a moderator-authenticated big-screen page showing the quiz title, plain-text full join URL, matching inline SVG QR code (`rqrcode`), live `"Players: N"` counter, `"Start"` / `"Finish"` / `"Next"` / `"End quiz"` controls, `"Question X of Y"` progress, live `"Answers: A / P"` active-player counter, per-option answer counts and `"Correct"` markers on reveal, and `"The quiz is over"` upon completion.
- **Player Experience & Security**: Built `/play/:code` with `"Your name"` / `"Join"` onboarding, `"Hi, <name>!"` waiting state, signed cookie persistence across browser re-opens, immediate option submission with `"Your answer"` marking (last pick counts while open), zero exposure of answer correctness in HTML/JSON/WebSocket payloads until `"Finish"`, live `"Correct!"` / `"Wrong!"` / `"No answer"` feedback, and `"The quiz is over"` blocking late joins after the game ends.
- **Real-Time & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience**: Powered live updates without page reloads via Action Cable (`SolidCable` in production), connection presence tracking, monotonic `state_version` guards, `bfcache` handling, retryable answer submissions, and automatic state resynchronization.
